title: USGS Event Summary v2 (Reviewed): M 8.9 — RCC Forward, 11:01

fields.issuer: USGS National Earthquake Information Center (forwarded by Oregon OEM Regional Coordination Center)
fields.title: M 8.9 - 80 km W of Port Alder, Oregon
fields.notes: Event summary version 2 (REVIEWED): M 8.9, revised from M 8.0 preliminary. ShakeMap version 2: estimated MMI IX at Port Alder and MMI VIII at Kellerton. PAGER version 2: RED alert for estimated fatalities and RED alert for estimated economic losses. Ground failure summary version 2: high estimated liquefaction along the Alder River estuary. All values are modeled estimates and will be revised as more data arrive. Duty Seismologist, RCC bridge line, 11:01 PDT: "Expect at least one more magnitude revision. Please quote the version number."
fields.footer: Forwarded to eoc@marlowcountyor.example by Oregon OEM RCC, 11:01 PDT, Tue 13 Apr 2027. EXERCISE PRODUCT. Not an official earthquake record.

instructorNote: Hand this out together with the PIO's unsent 10:50 draft Facebook post. The draft still reads "A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck off our coast...". Check three things: whether Command has the sitrep note the date and version of ShakeMap and PAGER v2 and keep the PAGER red estimate in a separate modeled column, apart from Sheriff, Fire and Public Works field reports (SOP-EQ-02 section 3); whether the Warning Coordinator sets "M 8.9 (USGS reviewed, v2, 11:01)" as the one magnitude for every channel; and whether the PIO corrects the draft without stating a PAGER loss figure as observed.

citations.quote: Within 30 minutes of a large earthquake the EOC reads, as estimates: the USGS earthquake event summary and magnitude; the ShakeMap shaking intensities; the PAGER loss estimate; and the ground failure

The National Tsunami Warning Center; the USGS National Earthquake Information Center and the Pacific Northwest Seismic Network; the National Weather Service forecast office in Portland; Oregon Emergen
